en.title: Final Fantasy VII: Ever Crisis Shutting Down October 6th, 2026
en.summary: Square Enix has announced the end of service for the mobile RPG Final Fantasy VII: Ever Crisis. The game will cease operations on October 6th, 2026, bringing a close to its reimagining of the FFVII saga.
en.body:
The world of **Final Fantasy VII** is about to lose another piece of its expanded universe. Square Enix has officially announced that **Final Fantasy VII: Ever Crisis** will be ending its service on October 6th, 2026. This news comes as a disappointment to many players who have been enjoying the mobile gacha title that aimed to bring the entirety of the **Final Fantasy VII** saga, including the original game, **Crisis Core**, and other related stories, into one cohesive experience with a charming, updated visual style.

Launched initially on iOS and Android in September 2023, with a PC release following in December 2023, **Ever Crisis** offered a unique way to relive iconic moments and explore new narratives within the **Compilation of Final Fantasy VII**. The game managed to garner significant attention, even reaching 7 million downloads before its PC debut. However, the decision to end service, as stated by Square Enix, comes after careful consideration, with the company finding it difficult to maintain the quality of experience players expect.

> "We understand that this news may be disappointing, and we sincerely apologize for the abrupt nature of this announcement," wrote Square Enix as part of its announcement. "Since the launch of the App Store and Google Play versions on September 7, 2023, and the Steam version on December 6, 2023, we have worked to provide the best possible experience for our players. After careful consideration, however, we have determined that it will be difficult to continue doing so and have made the decision to end service."

## The End of an Era for a Mobile Compendium

For fans of **Final Fantasy VII**, **Ever Crisis** represented a ambitious project to consolidate the sprawling narrative of their favorite characters and worlds. It allowed both long-time followers and newcomers to experience Cloud Strife's journey, Zack Fair's adventures, and more, all within a single, accessible platform. The game's gacha mechanics, while a staple of the mobile genre, also meant that player investment was tied to ongoing development and new content. The announcement of its shutdown suggests that these elements may not have met Square Enix's long-term goals for the title, or that the operational costs have become prohibitive.

## What This Means for Players

As of the announcement, players will no longer be able to purchase Red Crystals, the game's premium currency. However, all existing Red Crystals can be spent until the servers go offline. Planned in-game events will continue as scheduled until October 6th, 2026, giving players a final few months to enjoy the content. Square Enix has also confirmed that personal and account information will be deleted post-service, and players in Taiwan will be eligible for refunds on unused in-game currency, with further details to be released on the official website. The abruptness of the announcement has understandably left many players feeling disheartened, especially those who had invested significant time and resources into their accounts.

## Looking Ahead

With the end of service set for October 6th, 2026, players have a clear timeframe to conclude their adventures in **Final Fantasy VII: Ever Crisis**. While this chapter closes, the enduring legacy of **Final Fantasy VII** continues with other ongoing projects and the upcoming **Final Fantasy VII Rebirth**, ensuring that the beloved universe remains vibrant for fans.

content_raw: Square Enix has announced that it is ending support for Final Fantasy 7: Ever Crisis on October 6th. Leading up to the game’s servers being taken down, players will no longer be able to purchase any Red Crystals from the in-game store. However, they will be free to spend all the Red Crystals that they might have until the servers are taken down. In the meantime, planned in-game events will continue until October 6th. Square Enix has also said that it plans to delete all of the personal and account information it has from its players once the end-of-service process has been completed. Players residing in Taiwan will also be eligible for refunds on unused in-game currency. More details about these refunds will be revealed on the game’s official website at a later date. Final Fantasy 7: Ever Crisis was originally released on Android and iOS in September 2023 and on PC in December 2023 . The title was meant to be a way for players to experience iconic moments from the original release of Final Fantasy 7 and its prequel spin-off, Crisis Core: Final Fantasy 7 , in a new visual style. “We understand that this news may be disappointing, and we sincerely apologize for the abrupt nature of this announcement,” wrote Square Enix as part of its announcement. “Since the launch of the App Store and Google Play versions on September 7, 2023, and the Steam version on December 6, 2023, we have worked to provide the best possible experience for our players. After careful consideration, however, we have determined that it will be difficult to continue doing so and have made the decision to end service.” When it first came out, Final Fantasy 7: Ever Crisis saw quite a bit of success, with Square Enix confirming that the title had been downloaded 7 million times before even coming out on PC. At the time, it decided to reward players for their interest in the game by giving out a thousand Blue Crystals. In terms of gameplay, Final Fantasy 7: Ever Crisis featured a fast-paced command-based combat system based on the Active Time Battle system from the original Final Fantasy 7 . Players could make use of classic elements, including unique abilities, Materia, summons, and Limit Breaks. In the meantime, Square Enix is working on wrapping up its Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy with the release of Final Fantasy 7 Revelation in Spring 2027.
